summary: LUNA-VIEW is an interactive web-based application designed to help mission planners compare potential landing sites and mission dates near the Moon's south pole. It visualizes the positions of the Sun and Earth relative to the local lunar horizon to identify potential solar power generation periods and direct-to-Earth communication windows. Users can explore candidate landing locations, examine sunlight and Earth visibility, and compare different mission scenarios through an intuitive dashboard. By combining NASA scientific data, astronomical calculations, terrain information, and interactive visualizations, LUNA-VIEW aims to make complex lunar mission planning information easier to understand and evaluate for scientists, educators, students, and the public.
details: LUNA-VIEW is designed as an interactive lunar mission planning platform that helps users evaluate potential landing locations near the Moon's south pole. The application allows users to select candidate landing sites and mission dates and visualize the Sun's and Earth's positions relative to the local lunar horizon. The sunlight analysis helps identify periods when solar panels may receive sunlight, while the Earth visibility analysis helps identify potential direct-to-Earth communication opportunities. The main features include: 1. Landing Site Explorer – Explore and select candidate lunar landing locations. 2. Sunlight Simulator – Visualize solar elevation, azimuth, illumination periods and shadow conditions. 3. Earth Visibility Simulator – Examine Earth's position and potential communication windows. 4. Interactive Lunar Visualization – Explore the lunar environment through an interactive visual interface. 5. Site Comparison – Compare different landing sites and mission dates. 6. Mission Analysis – Present sunlight and communication opportunities to support landing-site selection. The proposed application uses HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the frontend, Three.js for 3D visualization, Python for scientific calculations, and NASA/JPL SPICE and NASA LOLA terrain data for astronomical and topographical analysis. The project's main innovation is combining sunlight availability, Earth visibility and landing-site comparison in one accessible interface. It aims to simplify complex scientific information and support better-informed lunar mission planning decisions.
